**Goal:** obtain one organized table of all core effects, understand its scale
and intervals, and export it without copying numbers from the console.

Use the [quick start](GetStarted.html) first if you have not fitted a model.
The short setup below makes this page independently runnable.

<details>
<summary>Example setup: create result</summary>


``` r
data(example_data)
result <- wsMed(
  data = example_data,
  M_C1 = c("A1", "B1"), M_C2 = c("A2", "B2"),
  Y_C1 = "D1", Y_C2 = "D2",
  form = "P", Na = "DE", ci_method = "mc",
  R = 2000, seed = 123, standardized = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
```

</details>

This example requests **standardized results** during analysis. The reports,
summary tables and generic plots below inherit that choice.

## Get the table you need


``` r
s <- summary(result)
knitr::kable(s$effects[c("label", "estimate", "std.error", "conf.low", "conf.high")],
  digits = 4, col.names = c("Effect / pathway", "Estimate", "SE", "CI lower", "CI upper"))
```



|Effect / pathway      | Estimate|     SE| CI lower| CI upper|
|:---------------------|--------:|------:|--------:|--------:|
|Direct effect         |  -0.1879| 0.1021|  -0.3878|   0.0191|
|M1                    |   0.0077| 0.0181|  -0.0284|   0.0464|
|M2                    |  -0.0066| 0.0149|  -0.0434|   0.0181|
|Total indirect effect |   0.0011| 0.0236|  -0.0471|   0.0464|
|Total effect          |  -0.1867| 0.1010|  -0.3836|   0.0112|



The rows cover the direct effect, each specific indirect effect, the total
indirect effect and the total effect. In a single-mediator model, the specific
and total indirect effects are equal; both named rows remain available.
`knitr::kable()` rounds only this display, while `s$effects` retains full precision.

| You want to... | Use |
|---|---|
| Read a core report in the console | `print(result)` |
| Include path coefficients in the report | `print(result, detail = "full")` |
| Save a statistical summary | `s <- summary(result)` |
| Get all selected effects as a data frame | `s$effects` or `as.data.frame(s)` |
| Get conditional path coefficients | `s$coefficients` |
| Check method, scale and confidence level | `s$info` |

`print()` displays a report and returns the original object invisibly.
`summary()` creates a structured result that you can save, filter and plot;
entering `s` displays its ordinary R coefficient tables. Neither repeats fitting
or sampling. With moderation, `$coefficients` contains slopes evaluated at the
selected moderator values; use `type = "parameters"` for primitive parameters.

## Check the scale and intervals


``` r
s$info[c("standardized", "method", "level")]
#> $standardized
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "mc"
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
```

For these complete condition effects, standardization divides the estimate by
the model-implied **marginal SD of the outcome difference**. It does not use a
separate denominator for each moderator value or category. See
[standardized effects](StandardizedModeratedMediation.html) for the definition
and conditional examples.


``` r
raw <- summary(result, standardized = FALSE)
raw$effects[c("effect", "estimate")]
#>           effect      estimate
#> 1             cp -0.0317954295
#> 2     indirect_1  0.0013113045
#> 3     indirect_2 -0.0011199168
#> 4 total_indirect  0.0001913877
#> 5          total -0.0316040417
```

The override affects this query only. `result` keeps its original preference.
Summary effect SEs come from the stored effect draws, and intervals are
percentile intervals. The older stored-table report may use a different
bootstrap interval convention; use the same convention when comparing reports.

## Select effects or change confidence level


``` r
indirect <- summary(result, type = "indirect")
indirect$effects[c("effect", "label", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
#>       effect label     estimate    conf.low  conf.high
#> 1 indirect_1    M1  0.007748230 -0.02841732 0.04635855
#> 2 indirect_2    M2 -0.006617359 -0.04340102 0.01810294
ci90 <- summary(result, level = .90)
ci90$effects[c("effect", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
#>           effect    conf.low   conf.high
#> 1             cp -0.35855010 -0.01925776
#> 2     indirect_1 -0.01725297  0.03875023
#> 3     indirect_2 -0.03386875  0.01227338
#> 4 total_indirect -0.03893181  0.03907865
#> 5          total -0.35092433 -0.02184333
```

Other choices are `type = "direct"`, `"total_indirect"`, `"total"`, `"paths"`
or `"parameters"`. `terms` selects identifiers listed in the `effect` column.
If the original analysis stored both engines (`ci_method = "both"`), select
`method = "mc"` or `"bootstrap"` in `summary()`; `print()` labels them separately.

For a moderated analysis, supply raw values with `at = list(Age = c(30, 50))`
or original category labels. Use your moderator's actual column name.
Without `at`, continuous moderators use their centering reference and
categorical moderators use all observed levels. These are **conditional effects**,
not effects averaged over the moderator. See the [analysis guide](AnalysisGuide.html#add-moderation).

## Compare two pathways


``` r
effects <- wsmed_effects(result)
difference <- wsmed_contrasts(effects,
  list(B_minus_A = c(indirect_2 = 1, indirect_1 = -1)))
as.data.frame(difference)[c("label", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
#>       label    estimate    conf.low  conf.high
#> 1 B_minus_A -0.01436559 -0.06651116 0.02999554
```

`B_minus_A` is the indirect effect through B minus the effect through A.
Its interval is computed from their matched joint draws. Do not subtract
confidence-interval endpoints or infer a difference merely because only one
of the separate intervals excludes zero.

## Export numbers and save a figure


``` r
write.csv(s$effects, "mediation-effects.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(s$coefficients, "path-coefficients.csv", row.names = FALSE)
p <- plot(s, title = "Standardized mediation effects")
ggplot2::ggsave("mediation-effects.png", p, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

The exported data retain full precision. CSV files include effect identifiers,
scale, inference method, confidence level and any moderator information.
The export examples write files to your working directory; change the names
before using them if those files already exist.
